prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 — For a Fair Deal

The Liberal Democrats argue that Conservatives have driven multiple crises: a broken NHS, a cost‑of‑living squeeze, housing shortages, sewage‑polluted rivers, and a damaged relationship with Europe. Their “Fair Deal” promises to transform British politics and deliver clean growth, world‑class public services, restored nature, and a stronger, more democratic UK.

Five pillars of the Fair Deal
- A fair economy: Invest in renewables and home insulation to cut bills and create secure, well‑paid jobs. Back small businesses, reform business rates into a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships and Lifelong Skills Grants, overhaul parental leave, fix the UK–EU trading relationship, and manage the public finances responsibly. Fund priorities by reversing Conservative bank tax cuts, imposing a proper windfall tax on oil and gas, and raising the Digital Services Tax. When affordable, raise the tax‑free personal allowance.
- World‑class public services: New rights to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent) with 8,000 more GPs; an NHS dentistry rescue plan; mental health hubs for young people and a qualified mental health professional in every school; a 62‑day maximum wait to start cancer treatment; stronger community policing and a guarantee that all burglaries are investigated; a repaired safety net with fair taxes.
- Climate and nature leadership: Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; a ten‑year home energy upgrade; a rooftop solar drive; decoupling electricity from gas prices; maintaining the fracking ban; transforming water companies into public benefit companies, banning sewage dumping, and creating a tougher regulator; Clean Air Act; “double nature” by 2050 and protect 30% of land and sea by 2030.
- A strong UK in a fairer world: Fix relations with Europe through a staged roadmap to remove trade barriers, deepen cooperation and ultimately seek to join the Single Market; stand up to authoritarianism, support Ukraine, restore aid to 0.7%, and provide safe, legal routes for refugees; advocate a ceasefire and a two‑state solution in Israel–Palestine.
- A truly fair democracy: Proportional representation for Westminster and English councils, caps on donations, scrap voter ID, reform the Lords, devolve power across the UK, uphold the Human Rights Act, and use citizens’ assemblies on major challenges.

Key policies across people’s lives
- Health and care: Invest in public health; free personal care across the UK; a Carers’ Minimum Wage (+£2/hour), a Royal College of Care Workers, paid carers’ leave and guaranteed respite; modernise cancer care and diagnostics; digital transformation that saves staff time and improves outcomes.
- Families, children and education: A mental health professional in every school; per‑pupil funding rising above inflation; a Tutoring Guarantee; expanded early years (extra free hours and a higher Early Years Pupil Premium); Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000 initially); day‑one parental rights, double Statutory Maternity and Shared Parental Pay, paternity at 90% pay, and a use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month; rejoin Erasmus Plus.
- Housing: Build 380,000 homes a year, including 150,000 social homes; new garden cities; zero‑carbon new homes; emergency retrofitting; ban no‑fault evictions; three‑year default tenancies; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders; end rough sleeping.
- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout, restore 2030 zero‑emission sales deadline, cut VAT on public charging; freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing, electrify more rail, deliver Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower local bus franchising; national active travel networks; fix local roads.
- Rights and equality: Make misogyny a hate crime; ban conversion therapy; scrap anti‑protest laws and live facial recognition; protect trans and non‑binary rights; Race Equality Strategy; flexible working as a right; stronger disability rights.
- Immigration and asylum: End the Hostile Environment; scrap the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme; three‑month standard for asylum decisions; allow work after three months; flexible work visas; reverse harsh family visa thresholds; protect EU citizens’ rights.
- Defence and security: Reverse Army cuts with an ambition above 100,000 regulars; increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; maintain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms export controls.

Overall, the Liberal Democrats promise competent economics, green prosperity, strong rights, internationalism and clean, accountable politics — a fair deal so everyone can get the care, opportunity and security they deserve.
